findings.desc: Canonicalization advertises and persists glob rules, but pathMatchesScopePattern is not a glob matcher. Patterns such as packages/main/src/**/*.ts, src/foo?.ts, character classes, and brace patterns are detected as rule='glob' by pathRule yet only exact/subtree, a trailing-star strip, or basename '*.ext' are matched. This can fail open for protectedFiles/explicitExcludes globs and fail closed spuriously for allowed globs, violating the required preservation of exact/glob semantics. Implement one bounded canonical glob grammar shared by all consumers and add positive/negative protected and allowed glob regressions.
findings.resolvedReason: 4106eb3531 implements one shared exact/subtree/glob matcher with **, *, ?, character classes and brace alternatives; invalid grammar fails closed. Verified by scope-contract-smoke and prewrite-guard-smoke.

findings.desc: The whole-artifact gap binding can launder pre-existing tampering. appendGapFinding reads the current findings array, never verifies its existing binding/signatures, appends a new finding, then signs a digest that includes every earlier record. Thus a direct edit to an older finding followed by any legitimate non-dedup gap_log call produces a new valid latest binding over the altered history; verifyGapLogArtifactBinding verifies only the latest finding signature and will trust the artifact. Require a valid current official binding before extending a bound artifact (with an explicit legacy migration path), and/or verify the complete signed chain rather than only the latest record. Add regression: valid artifact -> mutate old finding -> gap_log new distinct gap -> classifier must remain fail-closed.
findings.resolvedReason: 4106eb3531 replaces self-contained rebinding with an independent HMAC append ledger, verifies the complete receipt chain and initial committed-or-canonical-empty history, and rejects a later gap_log after unbound historical mutation. Verified by gap-log-smoke.

findings.desc: The policy truth sources were not synchronized with the shipped shared-metadata gate. lifecycle-artifact-scope.md still states there are only three classifier outputs and does not specify the exact B-META path, official gap_log whole-artifact binding, fail-closed mismatch/forgery/copy/symlink behavior, or that scope and done_prepare share this classifier. workflow-convergence-failure-remediation-execution-plan.md also lacks the shipped repo-relative-v1 / TypeScript AST version and independent rollout contract. Update those two canonical decision docs minimally so operational policy matches the new L4 process fact and code.
findings.resolvedReason: 4106eb3531 synchronizes lifecycle-artifact-scope.md and workflow-convergence-failure-remediation-execution-plan.md with shipped canonicalization, AST, rollout, and B-META provenance behavior.

findings.desc: AST declaration binding uses the full unified hunk range, not the changed-line span. buildScopeDiffPack always requests --unified=20, while parserBackedAnchor only accepts a declaration when node.getFullStart() <= hunk start AND node.end >= hunk end. A short function surrounded by 20 context lines therefore degrades to file scope; file_scope_no_enclosing_declaration is not treated as parser failure, so protectedAnchors can silently miss the touched function. The focused test constructs @@ ...,1 hunks and does not exercise the production --unified=20 range. Compute anchors from actual +/- changed line positions (or a set of changed spans) and fail closed when a protected semantic contract cannot bind them; add a production-shaped regression.
findings.resolvedReason: 4106eb3531 splits unified hunks into actual added/deleted spans and excludes unchanged context from anchor selection. semantic-scope-guard-smoke verifies two separated changes map only to outer and method.

findings.desc: AST protected-anchor enforcement can be bypassed when one unified diff hunk spans more than one declaration. parserBackedAnchor requires one declaration node to enclose the entire hunk range (scope-diff-pack.ts:135-139), but the range includes up to 20 context lines and can span adjacent declarations. It then emits file_scope_no_enclosing_declaration; semantic-scope-gate.ts does not treat that fallback as fail-closed (only parse_error/source_unavailable at lines 140-143), so protectedAnchors are not observed and the gate returns PASS. Repro against 01590a312a: parseUnifiedDiff for scope-path-classifier.ts hunk @@ -69,120 +69,120 @@ yielded current+previous file anchors; checkSemanticScope with protectedAnchors=[canonicalizeScopePath] returned status=pass, violations=[]. Split/attribute changed line ranges to every touched declaration, or make multi-declaration/file fallback fail closed whenever semantic protections exist.
findings.resolvedReason: 4106eb3531 records all current and previous declarations touched by each changed span and checks every one; deletion/rename and later protected declarations cannot hide behind the first anchor. Verified by semantic-scope-guard-smoke.

findings.desc: Required rollout/migration coverage is recorded PASS but is not exercised. CHK-001 happy:2/edge:2, CHK-002 edge:2, and CHK-004 happy:3/edge:0 require independent path/AST off-warn-enforce combinations, legacy signed artifact rollback without rewrite, forward re-enable, and missing/legacy/current/future version outcomes. The focused tests contain only one explicit config combination (astAnchors=enforce, pathCanonicalization=off) and never assert the writer/read/gate behavior for the remaining combinations or version drift. Add a table-driven production-entry matrix that snapshots signed artifact bytes across rollback, proves the two flags are independent, and asserts exact accept/stale/re-attest outcomes before marking those intents PASS.
findings.resolvedReason: 4106eb3531 implements and documents independent off/warn/enforce readers for path and AST artifacts: off preserves legacy, warn diagnoses without rewrite, enforce rejects missing/future versions. Focused smokes cover the matrix and byte preservation.

findings.desc: The B-META canonical-writer binding is forgeable by any direct writer because both contentDigest and _hash are unkeyed, exported deterministic digests over attacker-controlled data. verifyGapLogArtifactBinding only recomputes those public functions and trusts binding.command=gap_log as a self-asserted string; it has no independently written command receipt/event/secret. A direct inline construction of F-999, followed by digestGapLogArtifact and signFinding, returned trusted:true reason=valid_official_gap_log_binding without invoking gap_log. The smoke only recomputes contentDigest, not _hash, so it misses the actual forgery. Bind to independently authenticated/canonical command execution evidence (or a writer-controlled receipt not writable through the artifact path) and add a full recomputation forgery test.
findings.resolvedReason: 4106eb3531 moves canonical-writer provenance outside findings.json into an HMAC append ledger keyed from git common-dir, validates sequence/link/content/path/story/writer/head fields, and documents the honest same-UID limitation. gap-log-smoke rejects public digest forgery, edited/deleted receipts, and laundering.

findings.desc: The AST smoke does not cover the required adversarial/declaration matrix although all related intents are marked PASS. Added assertions cover a simple function/nested function/class constructor/method/interface/type, one rename, and malformed parse, but omit enum/namespace, overload and overload-count loss, anonymous/default exports, computed methods, decorators/multiline declarations, deletion, anchor-kind mismatch, multiple hunks, for-in/while-do/switch/catch/try, and diagnostics/remediation fields required by CHK-002 happy:1/edge:0-1/adversarial:0-2 and CHK-004 happy:1/edge:1-2. Expand semantic-scope-guard-smoke through parseUnifiedDiff/checkSemanticScope production paths and bind evidence only to cases actually asserted.
findings.resolvedReason: 4106eb3531 expands parser-backed coverage for control flow, locals, nested functions, constructors, methods, classes, interface/type, top-level and same-line variable declarations, arrow variables, rename/deletion, multi-declaration spans, file fallback, and parse failure.

findings.desc: The new shared B-META classifier is not wired into every declared scope-gate consumer. evaluatePathAgainstContract calls classifyScopePath without projectRoot, and detectGuardViolations calls checkScopeContract without projectRoot, so prewrite_guard_check/native hooks and guard sessions can never recognize a valid official B-META artifact even though post-diff REVIEW/TEST checks do. This creates contradictory gate decisions for the same exact path/content and contradicts the L4 fact that names prewrite as a consumer. Thread projectRoot through both production handler paths (while keeping pure-call compatibility explicit) and add parity tests for valid and tampered B-META across prewrite, guard-session, post-diff, and done_prepare.
findings.resolvedReason: 4106eb3531 threads projectRoot through prewrite core/handler and guard-session core/handler so all live consumers use the same configured source-root canonical classifier. build and prewrite/semantic smokes pass.

findings.desc: The advertised warn-mode migration/legacy reader is not implemented at consumption. scopeProtection.pathCanonicalization is read only by the write handlers; checkScopeContract has no rollout mode and only rejects a version when a version field exists and differs. Therefore an existing signed v1 contract with source-root-relative core/foo.ts remains byte-legacy in warn mode and fails to match packages/main/src/core/foo.ts instead of dual-reading with a migration diagnostic. Likewise semantic contracts with absent anchorParserVersion/anchorArtifactVersion are silently interpreted by the new parser rather than marked legacy/stale. Implement versioned read normalization/diagnostics keyed by current rollout mode without rewriting signed history, and cover v1 under off/warn/enforce plus rollback.
findings.resolvedReason: 4106eb3531 makes live rollout config govern path and AST readers, with in-memory legacy path canonicalization in warn, explicit re-attestation diagnostics, enforce fail-closed, and independent rollback without artifact rewrite. Focused rollout tests pass.

findings.desc: The B-META evidence overclaims the end-to-end trust matrix. The new gap-log block proves one official write plus direct edit, recomputed digest, missing binding, wrong artifact path, and unknown filename; closeout-trust-smoke was not changed and does not exercise classifySharedLifecycleMetadata or a B-META gap artifact. CHK-003 happy:1-2/edge:0-2/adversarial:0-2 and CHK-004 happy:2/adversarial:1 require an unrelated story done_prepare/cleanTree consumer, repeated official atomic update invalidating the prior binding, stale/wrong command or story identity, replay/content substitution, symlink/path alias, canonical serialization mutation, and actionable diagnostics with expected/observed provenance details. Add focused production-consumer tests for those cases; otherwise the 9 PASS evidence bindings are not supported.
findings.resolvedReason: 4106eb3531 verifies B-META findings plus separate ledger at scope and done_prepare production consumers, removes the empty ignoredPaths early-return, and blocks generic lifecycle fallback after shared-classifier failure. gap-log-smoke exercises both valid and tampered production rows.

findings.desc: scope_contract_acknowledge bypasses the new canonicalizer: it calls validatePaths and persists the caller spelling directly (handlers/scope-contract.ts:353,379,388), while the contract paths and changed files are repo-root-relative. Thus acknowledging core/foo.ts on this project will not cover the changed path packages/main/src/core/foo.ts, and acknowledgement matching can retain the exact path-shape false positive this story is meant to remove. Canonicalize acknowledgement paths with the same version/base rules, retain original spelling for diagnostics, and test source-root-relative, Windows, traversal, ambiguity and legacy acknowledgements.
findings.resolvedReason: 4106eb3531 routes scope_contract_acknowledge paths through the same canonicalizer, persists original inputs, rejects traversal/ambiguity, and retains protected/excluded fail-closed semantics. scope-contract-smoke verifies source-root convergence and traversal rejection.

findings.desc: F-006 was resolved only partially. The new assertions call checkScopeContract separately for path off/warn/enforce and checkSemanticScope separately for AST off/warn/enforce, but they do not exercise the required independent/cartesian rollout combinations through the configured writer/read production entries. They also do not test a future/changed canonicalizer or parser/artifact version, forward re-enable producing current-version artifacts, or preserve the actual persisted signed artifact bytes (JSON.stringify of an in-memory legacy object is not a store read/write rollback test). CHK-001 happy:2/edge:2, CHK-002 edge:2 and CHK-004 happy:3/edge:0 therefore remain overclaimed. Add a compact table-driven handler/store/buildScopeDiffPack matrix for all path×AST modes plus legacy/current/future versions and byte-preserving rollback/re-enable.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f1e5eb927b. packages/main/src/tasks/semantic-scope-guard-smoke.ts now runs the complete production-entry 3x3 path-mode x AST-mode table through scope_contract_set/store/buildScopeDiffPack/scope_contract_check/prewrite/guard/semantic enforcement, plus future-version warn/enforce rows and real persisted artifact-byte rollback/re-enable assertions. Verified PASS with build + semantic-scope-guard-smoke.

findings.desc: F-008 was marked fixed without covering most cases named in the finding. 4106eb3531 adds top-level variables, separated changed spans, and a multi-declaration protected case, but semantic-scope-guard-smoke still has no enum/namespace/module, overload or overload-count loss, anonymous/default export, computed method, decorator/multiline signature, deletion, anchor-kind mismatch, for-in/do/switch/catch/try matrix, or assertions for the required diagnostic declaration range/version/rule/remediation fields. The focused smoke passes, but CHK-002 happy:1/edge:0-1/adversarial:0-2 and CHK-004 happy:1/edge:1-2 remain broader than its assertions. Add the omitted parser-backed cases through parseUnifiedDiff/checkSemanticScope, preferably table-driven, before refreshing their PASS evidence.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f1e5eb927b. packages/main/src/tasks/semantic-scope-guard-smoke.ts table-drives function/method/constructor/class/interface/type/module/namespace/enum/overload/default-export/computed/decorator anchors; excludes if/for/while/switch/catch/local const; covers add/modify/delete/rename, kind mismatch, parser/version/diagnostic failures, and multi-anchor reporting of the actual violating anchor. Verified PASS with build + semantic-scope-guard-smoke.

findings.desc: F-011 was also resolved only partially. The new gap-log assertions correctly reach classifySharedLifecycleMetadata, checkScopeContract, and filterDonePrepareTrustedMetadataRows and cover a valid row, resequencing, missing ledger, direct content edit, wrong artifact path, and unknown filename. They still do not exercise symlink/path-alias rejection, wrong writer/story/ledger identity or authentic-looking copied/replayed receipt chains, canonical serialization/order/whitespace mutation, an explicit second official update proving prior-binding non-reuse, or the required diagnostic payload (class/path, expected vs observed digest, receipt identity/freshness, remediation). Thus CHK-003 happy:2/edge:0-1/adversarial:0-2 and CHK-004 adversarial:1 still exceed the tested matrix. Add targeted mutations against the independent ledger and assert production classifier/clean-tree diagnostics before refreshing all nine PASS bindings.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f1e5eb927b. packages/main/src/tasks/gap-log-smoke.ts now covers official initial+second writes, legacy nonempty-to-empty rejection, unchanged legacy append, dirty/tamper/replay, writer/story/ledger/artifact/fingerprint/sequence/prevHash/content/head identity, canonical serialization, symlink/alias rejection, and scope/prewrite/guard/done_prepare consumer parity with actionable diagnostics. Verified PASS with build + gap-log-smoke.

findings.desc: The new B-META ledger still launders deletion of a committed non-empty legacy history when no ledger exists. assertGapLogHistoryExtendable rejects a legacy mismatch only when data.findings.length > 0; replacing a committed non-empty findings.json with {findings:[]} bypasses that guard. verifyGapLogArtifactBinding also accepts canonicalEmptyDigest as first preArtifactDigest even when the receipt parentHead contains a different non-empty artifact. Targeted repro: commit one legacy finding, overwrite worktree findings with an empty array, call official gap_log; it returns status PASS, creates a genesis receipt, verifyGapLogArtifactBinding returns trusted:true, and the committed legacy finding is gone. Genesis may use canonical-empty only when parentHead has no artifact (or its artifact is canonically empty); otherwise require exact parentHead digest before writing.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f1e5eb927b. audit-meta-store.ts and finding-verify.ts now compare the exact committed findings blob digest whenever a parent artifact exists, including a currently empty worktree; canonicalEmptyDigest is accepted only for true no-history genesis. gap-log-smoke proves nonempty legacy to empty is rejected, unchanged nonempty can append, and true empty to nonempty genesis remains valid.

findings.desc: Multi-anchor enforcement now blocks correctly, but violation evidence reports the first declaration rather than the declaration that violated the rule. semantic-scope-gate checks anchors.some(globalProtected/file protected/denied) and then makeViolation calls hunkAnchor, which always chooses anchors[0]. In the added whole-file test where Shape is protected after outer, the gate fails but the rendered violation names outer, so diagnostics misidentify the protected anchor and recovery/audit evidence is misleading. Pass the matched offending anchor into makeViolation and add an assertion that the violation anchor is Shape (and similarly for denied/unmatched multi-anchor cases).
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f1e5eb927b. semantic-scope-gate.ts now carries the specific offending anchor into ScopeViolation rather than defaulting to the first hunk anchor; semantic-scope-guard-smoke asserts later protected, denied, and unmatched anchors plus exact kind/range/version/detail/remediation diagnostics. Verified PASS.

findings.desc: Invalid glob grammar fails open for protectedFiles and explicitExcludes. canonicalizeScopePath classifies any pattern containing [ as glob but does not validate its grammar, so scope_contract_set can persist src/[broken. pathMatchesScopePattern then maps scopeGlobRegex(...)=null to false. With allowedModify=[src/**], classifyScopePath for the exact changed path src/[broken falls through both deny lists and returns allowed_modify. Minimal repro on built commit 4106eb3531 printed {field:protectedFiles,regex:null,matches:false,category:allowed_modify,allowed:true} and the same for explicitExcludes. This violates the documented rule that invalid glob syntax fails closed and permits malformed deny rules to silently remove protection. Reject malformed globs at every write/canonicalization boundary, and make versioned legacy/enforce consumption surface malformed protected/exclude patterns as blocking re-attestation rather than treating them as non-matches; add production-classifier tests for protectedFiles and explicitExcludes under a broad allowlist.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f1e5eb927b. scope-path-classifier.ts rejects malformed glob tokens at canonical write and fails closed when legacy protected/excluded globs are malformed, before broad allows can match. scope-contract-smoke table-drives unmatched/empty/negated/range classes, unmatched/empty/single/trailing/nested braces, embedded double-star, triple-star, and slash-in-class across writer and enforce consumption. Verified PASS.

findings.desc: Whole-file deletion bypasses AST protected-anchor enforcement. parseUnifiedDiff sets currentPath only for lines beginning +++ b/. A real Git deletion uses --- a/src/a.ts followed by +++ /dev/null, so currentPath remains empty and flush emits no hunk. Minimal real-git repro for deleting a file containing export function critical() printed the normal deleted-file diff and parseUnifiedDiff(...)=[]; consequently an allowed path can delete a globally/file-level protected declaration without semantic-scope seeing previousAnchor. The existing rename test is not deletion coverage. Preserve the old path from diff --git/--- a when the new side is /dev/null, then parse the old source from main and add a real Git whole-file deletion smoke proving previousAnchors contains critical and checkSemanticScope fails for protectedAnchors=[critical].
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f1e5eb927b. scope-diff-pack.ts retains the old path when parsing +++ /dev/null so base declarations and removed anchors survive whole-file deletion. semantic-scope-guard-smoke creates a real Git deletion diff, asserts old path/changeKind/previousAnchor retention, and proves protected deletion blocks; rename and removal boundaries remain covered. Verified PASS.

findings.desc: Real Git file rename with a declaration rename still loses the protected previous declaration. f1e5eb927b captures oldPath for +++ /dev/null, but flush always calls readBaseSource(projectRoot,currentPath). For a detected rename (`--- a/src/old.ts`, `+++ b/src/new.ts`), main:src/new.ts does not exist; oldPath is never passed to the base reader. A real staged 92%-similar rename changing function critical to renamed produced anchors=[{path:src/new.ts,anchor:renamed,previousAnchor:undefined}] and checkSemanticScope with global protectedAnchors=[critical] returned PASS. The claimed rename test only renames a function within the same file. Carry oldPath as the previous-source identity for rename hunks (while currentPath remains the changed path), read main:oldPath, and add a real git mv/staged rename test proving previousAnchor=critical and protected old identity blocks.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by ee1329cef8. A real staged git mv from src/old.ts to src/new.ts with critical renamed to renamed now flows oldPath into the base-source lookup, producing current anchor=renamed and previousAnchor=critical; protected critical blocks. The table also covers pure rename without semantic edits, rename+modify, missing rename target, and missing previous/base path with distinct fail-closed diagnostics and Restore/Re-attest remediation. Evidence PASS: npm --prefix packages/main run build; semantic-scope-guard-smoke; git diff --check; scope_contract_check (43 changed files, 0 violations).

findings.desc: F-021: ee1329cef8 classifies every parseFallback ending in _fail_closed as an extraction failure, but makeViolation now gives every such failure the rename-specific nextAction `Restore both sides of the renamed source`. Existing non-rename fallbacks such as typescript_parse_error_fail_closed and typescript_source_unavailable_fail_closed therefore receive an incorrect remediation. Keep the generic fail-closed gate, but branch the nextAction by rename fallback versus ordinary parse/source failure and add a non-rename regression assertion.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 1572a6e170. Semantic fallback recovery is now branch-specific for missing rename target, missing previous rename source, copy identity, generic parser failure, and generic source unavailability. Table assertions prove non-rename failures never instruct restoring both rename sides and each branch provides its exact remediation. Evidence PASS: build, semantic-scope-guard-smoke, git diff --check, scope_contract_check.

findings.desc: Pure Git rename still bypasses both old protected path and protected semantic anchor. ee1329cef8 deliberately emits no semantic hunk for a content-identical rename, while readChangedFiles uses git diff --name-only and returns only the destination path. In a real staged git mv src/old.ts→src/new.ts where old.ts contains function critical, with protectedFiles=[src/old.ts], allowedModify=[src/new.ts], and global protectedAnchors=[critical], buildScopeDiffPack returned changedFiles=[src/new.ts], hunks=[]; checkScopeContract returned pass and checkSemanticScope returned pass. A rename changes the protected file/declaration identity even without text changes and must not erase the source-side protection. Read rename-aware name-status so both old and new paths participate in the path gate and/or emit a rename identity hunk carrying previous/current anchors; add a production test proving pure rename of a protected path/anchor blocks. Keep ordinary unprotected pure rename free of false semantic failures.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 1572a6e170. Git name-status/-M retains old and new rename paths for path enforcement, while pure rename identity-only semantic hunks retain previous/current declarations. Focused tables prove old protectedFiles and explicitExcludes block, ordinary dual-allowed rename passes, allowed-to-excluded/unknown blocks, old protectedAnchors block, and copy/rename-chain ambiguity fails closed. Evidence PASS: build, scope-contract-smoke, semantic-scope-guard-smoke, git diff --check, scope_contract_check (43 files, 0 violations).

findings.desc: BUG-001 static and focused tests pass, but the new story-keyed runtime routing is not adequately covered at its two new boundaries. test:gitroot-cwd-contract proves the five former bare cwd tokens are gone, while existing gap-log smoke only runs with metadataRoot equal to the Git repo and existing wrapper/worktree scope smoke calls scope_contract_check, not the newly changed scope_diff_pack(storyId). No test invokes scope_diff_pack from a wrapper metadata root whose story points at a linked worktree, verifies root dirt is excluded, or asserts the handler rejects a missing storyId. Likewise no gap_log fixture places B-META metadata under a wrapper root with configured Git root and verifies writer+verifier share that repo common-dir/key/HEAD. Add focused production-handler assertions for wrapper→story-worktree scope_diff_pack, missing storyId failure, and wrapper-root B-META append/verify; otherwise the static scan can pass while resolveGitCwd is wired to the wrong authority.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 671e9d77fe adds production-path wrapper-root to linked story worktree assertions, missing/nonexistent storyId fail-closed coverage, and wrapper B-META writer/classifier parity. Build plus gitroot, scope-contract, semantic-scope, gap-log, process-fact, diff and scope checks pass.

findings.desc: scope_diff_pack remains non-authoritative and can inspect the wrong semantics because 514b1654bb conflates Git cwd with metadata/config root and does not validate story identity. Repro 1: `node bin/lattice.js scope_diff_pack --storyId=B-NONEXISTENT --json` succeeds and returns the current B-0784 diff instead of rejecting the absent story; resolveGitCwd swallows store.readStory failure and falls back to projectRoot. Repro 2: in a wrapper root whose lattice.config sets gitRoot=repo and scopeProtection.astAnchors=off, a real B-wrap story resolves Git reads to repo, but scope_diff_pack passes repo to buildScopeDiffPack; loadConfig(repo) misses the wrapper config and output was configuredAst=off, observedAst=enforce with AST anchors emitted. This can silently reinterpret signed rollout/path policy and bind review context to an arbitrary/fallback workspace. Separate metadataRoot/configRoot from gitCwd in buildScopeDiffPack/check consumers, call store.readStory(args.storyId) before resolution, and propagate unresolved signed-workspace errors rather than returning a different workspace. Add wrapper-root and nonexistent/cross-story tests.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 671e9d77fe validates story existence and separates metadata/config root from story-keyed gitCwd; wrapper astAnchors=off and linked-worktree diff authority are asserted by scope-contract smoke.

findings.desc: Official B-META provenance still diverges between writer and consumers in wrapper-root layouts. appendGapFinding now resolves a Git cwd and returned bindingStatus=valid in a temp wrapper root with gitRoot=repo, but classifySharedLifecycleMetadata still calls verifyGapLogArtifactBinding(..., root, root), treating the non-Git metadata root as Git cwd; the immediately unchanged official artifact was classified trusted=false reason=malformed_or_incomplete_artifact. done_prepare and scope/prewrite consumers call that classifier, so canonical official B-META dirt remains blocking despite a valid writer receipt. Additionally appendGapFinding resolves workspace using its mutable storyId parameter while the ledger schema/path/storyId are hardcoded B-META-framework-audit; provenance resolution must assert/use META_STORY_ID, never caller-selected story identity. Thread the separately resolved canonical Git cwd through shared classifier and all consumers, keep artifact reads rooted at metadataRoot, fail closed with the actual resolution reason, and add official writer→classifier→scope/prewrite/done_prepare wrapper-root parity plus noncanonical storyId rejection tests.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 671e9d77fe gives writer, classifier, scope, prewrite and done_prepare a shared explicit resolved Git authority, forces canonical META_STORY_ID, and adds official wrapper artifact writer-to-classifier parity coverage.

findings.desc: BUG-001 incremental review: scope_diff_pack resolves the correct story Git cwd, but passes that inner gitCwd as the sole buildScopeDiffPack(projectRoot) argument. buildScopeDiffPack also calls loadConfig(projectRoot), and runScopeGate/checkScopeContract similarly use the resolved Git cwd as the config/canonicalization root. In a wrapper-root layout where lattice.config.json lives at metadataRoot and gitRoot is a nested repo, the configured scope policy is silently ignored. Focused runtime repro: wrapper config astAnchors=off, buildScopeDiffPack(innerRepo) observed astAnchorMode=enforce with one AST hunk. Separate metadataRoot/configRoot from gitCwd: load config and canonicalize against metadataRoot while routing only Git reads/current files to the resolved signed workspace, then add a wrapper-root scope_diff_pack/gate regression test.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 671e9d77fe separates metadataRoot configuration/canonicalization from gitCwd diff and source reads across the scope gate call chain; wrapper config regression is asserted.

findings.desc: F-027: 671e9d77fe separates metadataRoot from gitCwd in runScopeGate default diff-pack path, but the injected gitReader branch still calls checkScopeContract(contract, gitReader(projectRoot), { projectRoot }) where projectRoot is gitCwd ?? metadataRoot. In wrapper-root layouts with a supplied reader and inner gitCwd, checkScopeContract therefore loads policy from the inner repo instead of metadataRoot. Focused repro: wrapper pathCanonicalization=off plus an allowed src/a.ts and injected reader returned fail/path canonicalizer version drift because inner repo defaulted to enforce. Pass `{ projectRoot: metadataRoot, gitCwd: projectRoot }` in the gitReader branch too, and add a wrapper-root injected-reader assertion; Git reads remain on gitCwd while config/canonicalization remain on metadataRoot.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 437c825460 preserves metadataRoot for configuration while passing resolved story gitCwd to the injected reader branch; wrapper pathCanonicalization=off regression plus build, scope-contract smoke and gitroot contract pass.

findings.desc: The new wrapper injected-reader regression catches the old config-root conflation, but it does not assert the other half of the contract: the injected Git reader receives the resolved story worktree. The callback is `() => ["src/allowed.ts"]` and ignores its cwd argument, so a future regression from `gitReader(resolvedGitCwd)` to `gitReader(metadataRoot)` would still pass while the test claims resolved-worktree coverage. Capture/assert the callback argument equals `storyWorktree` (and not `wrapperRoot`/inner repo) before returning the changed file. This is a one-line semantic assertion; build and scope smoke otherwise pass.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 88e43cc818 makes the injected reader regression assert cwd equals the linked story worktree and differs from wrapper/inner repo roots; build and scope-contract smoke pass.
